title: SEEK EAGLE MODELING, ANALYSIS, AND TOOLS SUPPORT (SEMATS) 4
description: THE BELOW INFORMATION IS EXTRACTED FROM THE DRAFT PWS FOR THIS FUTURE SOLICITATION. WHILE THE INFORMATIOIN IS DEEMED ACCURATE WITH REGARDS TO THE SCOPE OF WORK REQUIRED, THE USG RESERVES THE RIGHT TO AMEND THE INFORMATION AND TASKS PRIOR TO THE OFFICIAL RELEASE OF THE RFP PWS. 1.0 DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES 1.1 General. This is a non-personnel services contract to provide SEEK EAGLE Modeling, Analysis, and Tools Support (SEMATS) 4 services to the U.S. Air Force SEEK EAGLE Office (AFSEO). The government shall not exercise any supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein. Such contract service providers shall be accountable solely to the contractor who, in turn is responsible to the government. 1.1.1 Description of Services/Objectives. The contractor shall provide all management, personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform SEMATS 4 as defined in this Performance Work Statement (PWS) except for those items specified as Government Furnished Property and services. The contractor shall meet the standards in this contract. This includes the planning, coordination, and surveillance of the activities necessary to ensure disciplined work performance and timely resources application to accomplish all tasks under the contract. The contractor shall be responsible for maintaining communication with the contracting officer (CO) and the contracting officer�s representative (COR), and to immediately notify both the CO and the COR of any problems that would prevent timely performance of this contract. The contractor is responsible for and required to implement, and maintain management control systems necessary to plan, organize, direct, and control all activities under this contract. 1.1.2 Scope. This Performance Work Statement (PWS) describes, in general, the required efforts under the SEMATS 4 Task Order (TO). The Contractor shall ensure that a broad range of expertise is available to support assigned tasks within mission responsibilities. The primary scope of the work is to provide software and data-based modeling, M&S, analysis, and tool and/or product development support. The scope includes professional engineering and technical support, management and non-technical support services for the AFSEO�s compatibility evaluation and mission planning processes and the development of M&S tools and products. The scope also encompasses network support services for an array of advanced M&S tools and high-performance computing resources as well as first line USAF Standard Desktop support. The SEMATS 4 scope does not include �inherently governmental functions� nor does it permit or include Personal Services. 1.2 Background. Air Force Pamphlet (AFPAM) 63-129, Chapter One, The SEEK EAGLE Program, defines the United States Air Force (USAF) standard process for aircraft-stores certification and designates the AFSEO as the organization responsible for managing all store certification activities. The mission of the AFSEO is to �deliver war-winning capability by expanding the compatibility of state-of-the-art stores on current and future generation aircraft, and by providing accurate combat weapon delivery software.� The AFSEO executes this mission by providing manpower, engineering tools, computer models and simulations, data, engineering rationale, and mission planning software applications necessary to safely load, carry, and employ inventory and developmental stores (e.g. weapons, tanks, pods) on fleet aircraft, along with the research and development necessary to influence follow-on aircraft and weapon system designs and production. Historically, the majority of the AFSEO mission has been focused on aircraft with externally carried weapon systems. As fifth-generation aircraft enter service and sixth-generation aircraft begin to materialize, the focus on carrying weapon systems in internal weapons bays will increase. In addition, weapon technologies continue to advance resulting in lighter weight weapons with complex geometric shapes, multiple aerodynamic surfaces, and advanced electronics. As these technologies mature and war-fighting capabilities increase, it becomes increasingly important to address aircraft-store compatibility issues. To understand the overall effects on aircraft performance and weapon employment characteristics due to advancing technology, extensive Modeling and Simulation (M&S), analyses, and test (both ground and flight), are required to assure safety-of-flight for the aircrew, weapon employment acceptability, and air worthiness. Expert skills and technological developments are needed to impact future aircraft and store designs/design changes for the purpose of providing maximum operational capability for the warfighter. The dynamic nature of the technical support requirements demands the availability of a workforce with flexibility and experience committed to accomplishing current tasks as well as the development of tools and models required to influence future aircraft weapon systems necessary to meet future challenges. The transfer of models, simulations, and tools from the aircraft original equipment manufacturer (OEM) to the AFSEO and the Contractor is essential for the research and development efforts necessary to determine solutions to future warfighter requirements. The Contractor shall be proficient in the continued research and development of these OEM products for the purpose of the investigation of possible solutions, the evaluation of solutions, and the documentation of solutions for future warfighter outcomes and capabilities. This PWS requires systems engineering, requirements analysis, design, and development of applicable models and simulations, which will integrate into higher level system elements for the purpose of producing aircraft weapon system solutions. Open air, ground and flight testing will be required to validate the model and simulation predictions required for improved warfighter capabilities. Additionally, research and development activity and products produced from the Contractor, in support of the AFSEO, influence the design, development, and manufacture of future aircraft weapon systems, as well as upgrades to fielded systems. 1.3 Inherently Governmental Function. The contractor shall not perform inherently governmental functions as defined in FAR Subpart 7.5 in relationship to this PWS. 1.4 Period of Performance. This is a five-year contract with 1 basic year and four option years. 1.5 Location and Hours of Work. Accomplishment of the effort contained in this PWS requires work at Contractor and Government facilities across various geographical locations (primarily in the continental United States (US)). The primary location of work is Eglin AFB FL. Normal workdays are Monday through Friday except US Federal Holidays. Workers normally work eight (8) hours per day, 40 hours per week. Flexible working hours (i.e. flextime) are permitted when performance is on-site, within the following guidelines: flextime workers shall not start earlier than 0600 and not later than 0900. Core hours of work are from 0900 to 1500 daily. All employees, whether working on-site or remotely, are expected to be available during core hours. Shortterm situations may make performance in excess of 8 hours per day, 40 hours per week necessary on occasion. The Contractor must ensure that they can provide for this contingency. 1.6 Tasks. title: Medium Unmanned Surface Vessel (MUSV) Phase II Integration and Testing
description: The Department of the Navy Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager (DRPM) / Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) for Robotics and Autonomous Systems (RAS) hereby issues this announcement regarding a forthcoming Area of Interest (AOI) for Medium Unmanned Surface Vehicles (MUSV) Phase II Integration and Testing. MUSV uses modular design principles to create adaptable and resilient solutions that can effectively counter evolving threats. We invite interested parties with expertise in innovative solutions to complex problems, vessel construction, autonomy, perception systems, and general maritime experience to participate in this opportunity. Vendors will be evaluated on platform maturity, open-architecture autonomy compatibility, endurance, payload integration capacity, and rapid-production scalability. To meet the critical operational demand signal for high-volume autonomous vessel procurement over the next decade, DRPM RAS will employ innovative and streamlined acquisition pathways. The government will leverage the authorities of 10 U.S.C. 3458 (Commercial Solutions) and 10 U.S.C. 4022 (Other Transactions) and intends to award Basic Ordering Agreements and prototype other transaction agreements, and potentially production contracts or transactions to successful vendors. To maintain technical superiority and capture rapid commercial innovations, DRPM RAS intends to issue the AOI with a rolling open window. This open call will allow new entrants to compete and existing vendors to submit updated product blocks and modular payload configurations. Approved platforms will be accepted into the maritime marketplace hosted on drones.mil. This digital clearinghouse will empower authorized acquisition authorities and operational stakeholders across the Department of War enterprise to rapidly configure and issue funded delivery orders for vetted maritime autonomous systems without redundant procurement cycles. Formal AOI release is planned on or before September 30, 2026. Detailed AOI instructions will be released via SAM.gov and syndicated at https://drones.mil. Interested industry vendors capable of delivering commercial or dual-use maritime unmanned surface systems are encouraged to ensure active SAM.gov registrations and monitor this notice for amendments, industry day announcements, and formal AOI documentation. All inquiries concerning this notice must be submitted in writing to the Agreements Officer at Christopher.j.murr.civ@us.navy.mil (note this email is distinct/different than the auto generated SAM.gov).

title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source American Society of Civil Engineers e-Journals
description: The US Army Corps of Engineers, Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC), intends to issue an award to American Society of Civil Engineers, 1801 Alexander Bell Drive, Reston, VA, 20191-4400, a sole source basis utilizing Simplified Acquisition Procedures as outlined in FAR Part 12. The requirement is for multiple physical site licenses for the following journals: American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE) Journal publications. The license is propriety to ASCE; ASCE Publications is the sole source provider of the complete ASCE Journals Online (1983-present), ASCE Proceedings Online, ASCE E-books and Standards, Civil Engineering Magazine, and GeoStrata Magazine collections. The ACS electronic titles are as follows: MSFEB40-Multisite Fee - E-books ALLP/ALLO-All ASCE Journals � Online PRAO-Online Proceedings w/ ALL Journals MSF/MSFERD-Multi-site license fee�ERDC EBST/EBST2025-2025 E-books and Standards Yearly Add-on The NAICS code for this requirement is 513120 with a size standard of 1000 employees. title: C1DA--657-27-209JB Renovate Main Lobby, Bldgs 1 & 53
description: 36C25527R0007 Pre-solicitation Notice Page 1 of 10 Pre-Solicitation Notice: Request for Architectural and Engineer SF330 Submission for Solicitation: 36C25527R0007, Renovate Building 1 & 53 Main Lobbies, Project No. 657-27-209JB. CONTRACT INFORMATION This A-E Services requirement is being procured in accordance with the Brooks Act (Public Law (PL0582) and implemented in accordance with the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 36.102. Firms will be selected for negotiation based on demonstrated competence and qualifications for the required work. This procurement is restricted to Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) firms. This is not a Request for Proposal, and an award will not be made with this announcement. This announcement is a request for SF 330 s from qualified Architectural and Engineer (A&E) contractors that meet the professional requirements. The selection criteria for this acquisition will be in accordance with the evaluation factors listed below. The completed SF 330 will be evaluated by the St. Louis-Jefferson Barracks (STL-JB) VAMC Evaluation Board and the selection report shall serve as the final selection list, which will be provided directly to the Contracting Officer. Negotiations will be conducted beginning with the most highly qualified firm. The Government will not pay nor reimburse any costs associated with responding to this request. The Government is under no obligation to award a contract as a result of this announcement. The most highly rated firm must physically come to the site and review the project before submitting a price proposal and letter of understanding at no cost to the government. The contract is anticipated to be awarded no later than December 30, 2026. Award of any resultant contract is contingent upon the availability of funds. Personal visits to discuss this announcement will not be allowed. The NAICS Code for this procurement is 541310, Engineering Services and the small business size standard of $12.5 Million. Award of a Firm Fixed Price contract is anticipated and award time for completion of design of this project is approximately 199 calendar days including time for VA reviews. The A/E firm shall also be required to perform construction period services if award of a construction project contract is made. DATABASE REGISTRATION INFORMATION: Verification of status of apparently successful offeror this acquisition is 100% set-aside for qualified service-disabled veteran owned small business A/E firm s incompliance with VAAR 852.219-73. Only businesses listed as certified in the SBA certification database at https://veterans.certify.sba.gov/, shall be considered. SYSTEM FOR AWARD MANAGEMENT (SAM.GOV): Federal Acquisition Registrations require that federal contractors register in the System for Award Management (SAM.GOV) database at https://sam.gov/content/ and enter all mandatory information into the system. Award cannot be made until the contractor has registered. Offerors are encouraged to ensure that they are registered in SAM.GOV prior to submitting their qualifications package. THE EXCLUDED PARTIES LIST SYSTEM (EPLS): To ensure that the individuals providing services under the contract have not engaged in fraud or abuse regarding Sections 1128 and1128A of the Social Security Act regarding federal health care programs, the contractor is required to check the Excluded Parties List System (EPLS) located at https://sam.gov/content/ for each person providing services under this contract. Further the contractor is required to certify that all persons listed in the qualifications package have been compared against the EPLS list and are NOT listed. During the performance of this contract the Contractor is prohibited from using any individual or business listed on the List of Excluded Individuals/Entities. E-VERIFY SYSTEM: Companies awarded a contract with the federal government shall be required to enroll in E-Verify within 30 days of the contract award date. They shall also need to begin using the E-Verify system to confirm that all their new hires and their employees directly working on federal contracts are authorized to legally work in the United States. E-Verify is an Internet-based system that allows an employer, using information reported on an employee's Form I-9, to determine the eligibility of that employee to work in the United States. There is no charge to employers to use E-Verify. (FAR 52.222-54) Qualified A-E firms are required to respond if interested by submitting one (1) original completed Standard Form 330 qualification package Parts I and II to include all consultants (form available on-line at: http://www.gsa.gov/portal/forms/download/116486).� Must include in Part I Section H an organizational chart of the firm (excludes consultants) and a design quality management plan. Submission information incorporated by reference is not allowed. All submissions must be in pdf format and emailed. Email subject line shall clearly identify Solicitation number: 36C25527R0007 and project name, Renovate Building 1 and 53 Main Lobbies, Project No.657-27-209JB. Responses must be received by 12:00 PM Central on October 30, 2026 via e-mail to the Contracting Officer at maria.hoover@va.gov. The 330 submissions must be a pdf document and must not exceed 10 MB. The A/E Firm must provide Basic Professional Services as delineated in the Scope of Work. As part of the Basic Professional Services, STL-JB VAMC Engineering Service expects the following primary A/E disciplines to be included: Project Manager, Supervisory, Architect, Electrical Engineer, Mechanical Engineer, Structural Engineer, Fire Protection Engineer, Certified Professional Industrial Hygienist, Plumbing Engineer, Life Safety Engineer, and Cost Estimator. Interested firms shall be required to respond to additional announcements separately from this announcement without further notice from the Government when posted to the Contract Opportunities website at https://sam.gov. The Contract Opportunities website is the only official site to obtain these documents. Additional information about this project will be issued on the System for Award Management website https://www.sam.gov/content/opportunities once available. PROJECT INFORMATION This project will renovate the main lobbies in B1 & B53 and improve veteran experience. The finishes are beyond their useful life and do not provide a welcoming intuitive way of finding experience for veterans and guests. Project will focus on replacement of existing architectural finishes (Floors, walls {including handrails & wall protection}, and ceilings) in public areas to include main entrances, canopy, elevator lobbies, and waiting rooms. This project will renovate approximately 4,000 DGSF in B1 First Floor Center at and 2300 DGSF located in B53. Scope of work will also include a reimagined entrance canopy at B1. Note: The Veterans Administration Medical Center at Jefferson Barracks is listed in the National Register of Historic Places (NRHP) as a historic district. Any work done on the exterior of Building will need to be reviewed with the Missouri State Historic Preservation Office. title: SEEK EAGLE MODELING, ANALYSIS, AND TOOLS SUPPORT (SEMATS) 4
description: EDITED (20260730): After reviewing the extract from the draft PWS, vendors interested in responding to this sources sought announcment should send a statement of interest that broadly matches their own capabilites and already-demonstrated experience to those services shown below. While links to your company's website are appreciated, your response should not simpy refer us to your website. THE BELOW INFORMATION IS EXTRACTED FROM THE DRAFT PWS FOR THIS FUTURE SOLICITATION. WHILE THE INFORMATIOIN IS DEEMED ACCURATE WITH REGARDS TO THE SCOPE OF WORK REQUIRED, THE USG RESERVES THE RIGHT TO AMEND THE INFORMATION AND TASKS PRIOR TO THE OFFICIAL RELEASE OF THE RFP PWS. 1.0 DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES 1.1 General. This is a non-personnel services contract to provide SEEK EAGLE Modeling, Analysis, and Tools Support (SEMATS) 4 services to the U.S. Air Force SEEK EAGLE Office (AFSEO). The government shall not exercise any supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein. Such contract service providers shall be accountable solely to the contractor who, in turn is responsible to the government. 1.1.1 Description of Services/Objectives. The contractor shall provide all management, personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform SEMATS 4 as defined in this Performance Work Statement (PWS) except for those items specified as Government Furnished Property and services. The contractor shall meet the standards in this contract. This includes the planning, coordination, and surveillance of the activities necessary to ensure disciplined work performance and timely resources application to accomplish all tasks under the contract. The contractor shall be responsible for maintaining communication with the contracting officer (CO) and the contracting officer�s representative (COR), and to immediately notify both the CO and the COR of any problems that would prevent timely performance of this contract. The contractor is responsible for and required to implement, and maintain management control systems necessary to plan, organize, direct, and control all activities under this contract. 1.1.2 Scope. This Performance Work Statement (PWS) describes, in general, the required efforts under the SEMATS 4 Task Order (TO). The Contractor shall ensure that a broad range of expertise is available to support assigned tasks within mission responsibilities. The primary scope of the work is to provide software and data-based modeling, M&S, analysis, and tool and/or product development support. The scope includes professional engineering and technical support, management and non-technical support services for the AFSEO�s compatibility evaluation and mission planning processes and the development of M&S tools and products. The scope also encompasses network support services for an array of advanced M&S tools and high-performance computing resources as well as first line USAF Standard Desktop support. The SEMATS 4 scope does not include �inherently governmental functions� nor does it permit or include Personal Services. 1.2 Background. Air Force Pamphlet (AFPAM) 63-129, Chapter One, The SEEK EAGLE Program, defines the United States Air Force (USAF) standard process for aircraft-stores certification and designates the AFSEO as the organization responsible for managing all store certification activities. The mission of the AFSEO is to �deliver war-winning capability by expanding the compatibility of state-of-the-art stores on current and future generation aircraft, and by providing accurate combat weapon delivery software.� The AFSEO executes this mission by providing manpower, engineering tools, computer models and simulations, data, engineering rationale, and mission planning software applications necessary to safely load, carry, and employ inventory and developmental stores (e.g. weapons, tanks, pods) on fleet aircraft, along with the research and development necessary to influence follow-on aircraft and weapon system designs and production. Historically, the majority of the AFSEO mission has been focused on aircraft with externally carried weapon systems. As fifth-generation aircraft enter service and sixth-generation aircraft begin to materialize, the focus on carrying weapon systems in internal weapons bays will increase. In addition, weapon technologies continue to advance resulting in lighter weight weapons with complex geometric shapes, multiple aerodynamic surfaces, and advanced electronics. As these technologies mature and war-fighting capabilities increase, it becomes increasingly important to address aircraft-store compatibility issues. To understand the overall effects on aircraft performance and weapon employment characteristics due to advancing technology, extensive Modeling and Simulation (M&S), analyses, and test (both ground and flight), are required to assure safety-of-flight for the aircrew, weapon employment acceptability, and air worthiness. Expert skills and technological developments are needed to impact future aircraft and store designs/design changes for the purpose of providing maximum operational capability for the warfighter. The dynamic nature of the technical support requirements demands the availability of a workforce with flexibility and experience committed to accomplishing current tasks as well as the development of tools and models required to influence future aircraft weapon systems necessary to meet future challenges. The transfer of models, simulations, and tools from the aircraft original equipment manufacturer (OEM) to the AFSEO and the Contractor is essential for the research and development efforts necessary to determine solutions to future warfighter requirements. The Contractor shall be proficient in the continued research and development of these OEM products for the purpose of the investigation of possible solutions, the evaluation of solutions, and the documentation of solutions for future warfighter outcomes and capabilities. This PWS requires systems engineering, requirements analysis, design, and development of applicable models and simulations, which will integrate into higher level system elements for the purpose of producing aircraft weapon system solutions. Open air, ground and flight testing will be required to validate the model and simulation predictions required for improved warfighter capabilities. Additionally, research and development activity and products produced from the Contractor, in support of the AFSEO, influence the design, development, and manufacture of future aircraft weapon systems, as well as upgrades to fielded systems. 1.3 Inherently Governmental Function. The contractor shall not perform inherently governmental functions as defined in FAR Subpart 7.5 in relationship to this PWS. 1.4 Period of Performance. This is a five-year contract with 1 basic year and four option years. 1.5 Location and Hours of Work. Accomplishment of the effort contained in this PWS requires work at Contractor and Government facilities across various geographical locations (primarily in the continental United States (US)). The primary location of work is Eglin AFB FL. Normal workdays are Monday through Friday except US Federal Holidays. Workers normally work eight (8) hours per day, 40 hours per week. Flexible working hours (i.e. flextime) are permitted when performance is on-site, within the following guidelines: flextime workers shall not start earlier than 0600 and not later than 0900. Core hours of work are from 0900 to 1500 daily. All employees, whether working on-site or remotely, are expected to be available during core hours. Shortterm situations may make performance in excess of 8 hours per day, 40 hours per week necessary on occasion. The Contractor must ensure that they can provide for this contingency. 1.6 Tasks. title: RFB to Lease the Stow-Hardy House at Minute Man National Historical Park
description: Summary of the Opportunity This Request for Bids (RFB) provides the opportunity for interested individuals and organizations to submit bids to the National Park Service (NPS) to lease NPS property for residential use (single family) at Minute Man National Historical Park under the following general terms and conditions. See attached �Draft Lease� for complete terms of occupancy. Property Offered for Lease Stow-Hardy House The Stow-Hardy house is located at 965 Lexington Road, Concord, Massachusetts, 01742. It is approximately 2,400 Sq. Ft with 3 bedrooms and 2.5 bathrooms and is situated on an approximately 0.4-acre landsite. The colonial style home was built circa 1786 and has been completely restored and renovated while retaining its original central arch chimney, oak timber framing, cedar shingle roof, and historic siding. The house has had significant mechanical upgrades including new plumbing, septic, heating, and electrical systems as well as a new smart washer and dryer. The kitchen features new stainless-steel appliances and a central island with farmhouse sink. The historic Battle Road Trail is located nearby, behind a mature Black Walnut grove. The trail is used year-round and provides the opportunity for various outdoor activities and connects the historic towns of Concord and Lexington. Uses of the Leased Property This lease is most suitable for low-impact, non-transient, residential occupancy of the house. The lessee is authorized to use the property as an occupant of the house and must be willing to become a part of the National Historical Park�s relationship with the public by maintaining the historic and well-tended appearance of the structure and grounds. In accordance with the attached draft lease, the lessee is responsible for all utilities and routine maintenance. The lessor will perform basic maintenance of the property as described in the lease. Term of Lease The lease will have a maximum term of three years. Lessee termination rights (termination without cause) will begin 90 days before the end of the first year of the lease and continue until the lease expires. Please note: 90 days� notice is required for termination without cause. Fair Market Value Rent The lessee will be required by the lease to pay at least fair market value rent to the NPS. Based on the terms included in the attached Lease (Section 5. Rent), the fair market value rent has been determined to be $51,600 annually, payable in equal monthly installments of $4,300 each month. The lessee shall pay to the United States as rent the sum of Fifty-One Thousand Six Hundred Dollars ($51,600) per year as the base rent payable to the National Park Service and forwarded by the lessee to the Superintendent, Minute Man National Historical Park. Rent checks will be mailed to Minute Man National Historical Park, 174 Liberty Street Concord, MA 01742, attention Superintendent. The annual rent shall be paid on the 1st day of each month in advance monthly installments of Four Thousand Three Hundred Dollars ($4,300). Payment covering the first month will be submitted with the executed lease. Other Terms and Conditions None. Competitive Process This lease opportunity is open to all interested persons on a competitive basis. The bidder submitting a responsive bid offering the highest monthly rent will be selected for award of the lease (subject to a determination of financial capability and reference check). A responsive bid is a bid that meets the material terms and conditions of this request for bids (see attached lease terms). The bid must offer a rental amount that is no less than fair market value described in the Fair Market Value Rent section of this RFP. If two or more bids are equal, a drawing shall make the lease award by lot limited to the equal responsive bids received. Initial and Rolling Bid Submissions Bids must be received by the date listed on the first page of this RFB and must be submitted electronically in the format provided on the following pages. A public bid opening will occur the next day after the Initial Bid Submission Deadline. If a winning bid is not selected on that date, the NPS will open bids every following Monday at 1:00 PM until a responsive bid has been submitted or until NPS terminates the solicitation. Authority This RFB is issued under the authority of federal law and regulations. The applicable law is found in United States Code at 54 USC 1021 and leasing regulations may be found in the Code of Federal Regulations at 36 CFR Part 18. This RFB and the offered lease are subject to and incorporate all terms and conditions of Part 18 as applicable. In the event of any conflict between the terms of this RFB and Part 18, Part 18 controls. For Further Information Please Contact: Mike McCarthy Administrative Officer Minute Man National Historical Park 174 Liberty Street Concord, MA 01742 Phone: (781) 472-0970 E-mail: mike_mccarthy@nps.gov NPS reserves the right at any time and in NPS� sole discretion, to cause or do any or all of the following: Waive or correct any defect or technical error as to form or content of this RFB or in any bid, response, proposal, or proposal procedure, as part of the RFB or any subsequent selection and negotiation process. Modify, amend, cancel, or suspend any and all aspects of the RFB and selection process. Reissue an RFB. Modify the scope of the Lease or the required responses or modify the components of the Lease. Request that Respondents clarify, supplement, or modify the information submitted. Extend deadlines for accepting RFB responses, or request amendments to responses after expiration of deadlines. Consider comparable projects owned, developed, or operated by a Respondent. The National Park Service and Minute Man National Historical Park The National Park Service and its Mission America�s National Park Service was created by Congress to �conserve the scenery and the natural and historic objects and the wildlife therein, and to provide for the enjoyment of the same in such a manner and by such means as will leave them unimpaired for the enjoyment of future generations.� Additionally, the Congress has declared that the National Park System should be, �� preserved and managed for the benefit and inspiration of all the people of the United States.� The National Park Service has as its overall mission the preservation and public enjoyment of significant aspects of the nation�s natural and cultural heritage. To learn more about the National Park Service, visit our website at www.nps.gov. This site includes information about who we are, our mission, NPS policies and individual parks. Minute Man National Historical Park Minute Man National Historical Park was created by an Act of Congress on September 21, 1959 �� to preserve for the benefit of the American people certain historic structures and properties of outstanding national significance associated with the opening of the War of the American Revolution�� The specific purposes of the park include: �� the preservation of the historic landscape along the road between Lexington and Concord, (2) sites associated with the causes and consequences of the American Revolution, and (3) the Wayside on Lexington Road in Concord �.� To learn more about Minute Man NHP visit our website at: https://www.nps.gov/mima/index.htm. Bid Submission Requirements In accordance with the Code of Federal Regulations � 36 CFR Part 18.7(b) which governs how lease proposals are solicited under an RFB, NPS specifies that bids must be in the form of a single PDF file and submitted electronically to mike_mccarthy@nps.gov. title: AN/ALE-47 Common Carriage Production IDIQ
description: DISCLAIMER: THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. INTRODUCTION: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR) at Patuxent River, MD announces its requirement to procure production-representative, flight-certified hardware to transition the AN/ALE-47 Common Carriage (CC) Countermeasures Dispensing System from the Engineering and Manufacturing Development (EMD) phase into rate production. This modernization program replaces the legacy AN/ALE-47 round-magazine dispenser system with a modernized, square-magazine architecture. This allows the Navy to deploy standard 1"x1"x8" square expendable countermeasures, expanding aircraft magazine capacity from 30 to 48 rounds and aligning joint logistics with the USAF, US Army, and F-35 platforms. The contract will cover the manufacture, testing, and delivery of the following Weapon Replaceable Assemblies (WRAs) and associated Support Equipment: SA-2669A/ALE-47(V) Common Carriage Sequencer: Modernized electronic control unit with upgraded processing, firmware loading capabilities, and increased memory to support the legacy dispenser, as well as next-generation intelligent expendables. D-74/ALE-47(V) Common Carriage Dispenser Housing Assembly: Ruggedized mechanical housing that mounts to the aircraft structure to secure the magazine assembly. MX-12772/ALE-47(V) Common Carriage Magazine Assembly: Upgraded high-capacity magazine capable of holding 48 individual 1"x1"x8" square expendable cartridges (a 60% capacity increase over legacy systems). AN/ALM-300 Support Equipment: Next-generation Organizational-Level (O-Level) flight line test sets. The estimated contract value will be $104,000,000.00 across United States Navy and Marine Corps. The proposed class of contracting actions will procure an estimated range of 114 - 186 shipsets per year for Fiscal Year (FY)28 through FY30 to satisfy the requirement. THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. It is a market research tool being used to determine potential and eligible businesses capable of providing the services described herein prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a Request for Proposal. The Government is not obligated to and will not pay for any information received from potential sources as a result of this notice. ELIGIBILITY: The Product/Service Code (PSC) for this requirement is 5865: Electronic Countermeasures, Counter-countermeasures and Quick Reaction Capability Equipment. All interested businesses are encouraged to respond. ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: This contract is planned to contain a three (3) year ordering period to satisfy requirements for FY28 through FY30. The anticipated award date is May 2028. The Government anticipates end item deliveries will commence as early as 12 months after each contract delivery order award. Initial production is anticipated to be an estimated 10 shipsets per month. ANTICIPATED CONTRACT TYPE: The contract type for this effort is anticipated to be a Firm Fixed Price Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract. PROGRAM BACKGROUND: The legacy countermeasure dispensing systems across the Navy fleet are limited by 1980s computer processing architectures and a proprietary round-magazine design with a capacity of 30 expendables. The Common Carriage (CC) program modernizes this critical survivability suite. By upgrading to square expendable geometry, the Navy streamlines its global supply chain with joint partners and paves the way for advanced, intelligent expendables (e.g., active radio-frequency expendables). Additionally, the system increases the capacity from 30 expendables to 48 expendables. The system also modernizes sequencing, upgrading the processing power and communication datalinks. This program is transitioning out of Engineering and Manufacturing Development (EMD) and entering production to outfit fleet deployers. REQUIRED CAPABILITIES: Interested sources must demonstrate qualified capability, active facilities, and certified quality controls (such as AS9100) to execute: Flight-Critical Electronic WRA Assembly & Quality Control: Demonstrated capability to manufacture, assemble, and test flight-critical electronic systems and Circuit Card Assemblies (CCAs) in accordance with a certified aerospace quality management system (AS9100 or equivalent). The vendor must demonstrate experience producing high-reliability avionics designed to withstand severe thermal, shock, and vibration operational environments. Precision Mechanical & Structural Castings: Production of thin-walled aluminum castings (D-74 Housing) and machined blocks (MX-12772 Magazine) to withstand maritime environments and carrier-landing shock. Production Environmental Stress Screening (ESS) & ATP: Execution of 100% throughput of Acceptance Test Procedures (ATP) and ESS (Random Vibration and Thermal burn-in/cycling) to isolate manufacturing defects. Firmware/Software Loading and Configuration Control: Secure loading, verification, and configuration management of Government-provided Operational Flight Programs (OFP) onto the non-volatile memory of the SA-2669A Sequencer. Supply Chain & Long-Lead Time Management: A demonstrated capability to manage and mitigate long-lead time material procurement for critical microelectronic components, with a supply chain structure that can support a 12-month post-award initial delivery schedule Counterfeit Part Prevention and Material Traceability: A documented and verifiable counterfeit part prevention and detection system compliant with DFARS 252.246.7007 and 7008. The System must ensure full material traceability for all components and critical hardware back to the original component manufacturer. Interested businesses shall demonstrate that your company currently possesses or has authorized access to the necessary technical data, or has a viable plan to obtain, generate, or otherwise secure the necessary technical data, and that it will be maintained throughout the duration of the effort being solicited. Interested businesses shall demonstrate the capability to complete the requirement within the Government�s required timeline. You may also submit information that demonstrates how you could potentially meet this requirement for future production opportunities. SUBMISSION DETAILS: Interested businesses shall submit a brief capabilities statement package (no more than twelve (12) 8.5 x 11 inch pages, font no smaller than 12 point, 1.5 line spaced) demonstrating their ability to perform the requirements described herein. In addition to these requirements, interested businesses shall adhere to the following submission instructions: 1. Document Type: Microsoft Word 2. Delivery: The capability statement package shall be sent by electronic mail (email) to Elizabeth V. Lamb at elizabeth.v.lamb2.civ@us.navy.mil. 3. Response Date: Submissions must be received via email no later than 1:00 p.m. Eastern Standard Time on 30 October 2026. 4. No classified information shall be submitted in response to this Sources Sought. 5. Questions or comments regarding this notice may be addressed to Elizabeth Lamb at the above email address. No phone calls will be accepted. 6. All responses shall include Sources Sought Notice name/number, Company Name, Company Address, Company Business Size, Cage Code, and Points-of-Contact (POC) including name, phone number, and email address. 7. title: Juvenile Services within the area of Garza County, Texas
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons (Bureau) is seeking concerns having the ability to provide Secure Juvenile Services (in-house beds) for juvenile, male and female, offenders Federal offenders within the area Garza County, Texas held under the authority of various United States statutes. The Secure Juvenile Services shall be in accordance with the Federal Bureau of Prisons Statement of Work entitled, "Juvenile Secure SOW March 2025�. This will be an indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity type contract with firm fixed unit prices for all line items. The In-House requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum of 13 beds and an estimated maximum of 20 beds, to be filled with any combination of males and females for the One-year Base Period and each of the Four One-year Option Periods. It is the intent of the Government to award a single provider, as these services are interconnected and rely upon each other to ensure adequate programming and case management of offenders. The Government reserves the right to potentially make an award which is deemed to be in the best interest of the Government. The closing date of RFP 15BRRC26R00000006 will be on or about October 30, 2026 at 2:00pm EST. All responsible sources may submit a proposal which will be considered by this agency. No collect calls will be accepted. Proper controls shall be used to prevent melt through or burn through. For aluminum, filler for welding 6061 alloy shall be 4043: filler for welding 5000 series alloys to themselves or to 6061 shall be 5356 or 5556. In addition,welding and weld inspection shall include: (1) Visual inspection shall include 5X (5power) magnification when a suspect condition is to be examined beyond the capability of normal vision. (2) Critical and major welds may be subjected to further non destructive testing (such as dye penetrant inspection)as prescribed by the buying activity. (3) Proper documentation shall be available for review by Government personnel. 3.2 WORK INSTRUCTIONS. Work instructions shall be posted at theoperator's work station giving procedures to control the welding process, i.e., filler material, weld size, electrical and gas characteristics, including flow rate. 3.3 MATERIALS AND MATERIALS CONTROL. The quality program shall assure that the materials used in fabrication or processing, i.e., base metals and weld filler material, be inspected and conform to the applicable physical, chemical and other technical requirements (supplier's certification is sufficient). 3.4 CONTROLS. Weld filler materials shall be clearly identified and segregated from each other both when in storage and at the work station. Work station environment shall be controlled to prevent conditions adverse to proper gas shielding. 3.5 CLEANING. Parts to be welded shall be cleaned to remove surface soils such as oils, waxes, grease, inks, etc. except that uninhibited alkaline solutions such as sodium hydroxide shall NOT be used. 3.6 DEOXIDIZING. The cleaned parts shall be chemically deoxidized NO MORE THAN 10 DAYS PRIOR TO WELDING to remove thick surface oxide films. (If the material or work is exposed to an outdoor environment, this time limit shall be reduced to a maximum of 3 days, to account for atmospheric effects.) Mechanical cleaning methods shall be applied just prior to the actual start of welding, to remove any reoxidation or residual thin oxide films. 3.6.1 CHEMICAL TREATMENT. An acid deoxidizing treatment shall be applied by either immersion or brushing/wiping. Deoxidizers acceptable for use shall include nitric acid, sulfuric chromic, phosphoric chromic, or equivalent solutions. Sodium hydroxide solutions shall not be used. Care shall be taken to assure 100% solution coverage of the area to be welded. To allow an adequately sized deoxidized area for good welding, the solution shall be applied to an area extending at least 2 inches from the weld site, or ending at any closer adjacent edge. 3.6.2 MECHANICAL MEANS. Immediately prior to welding, mechanical cleaning methods shall be applied to the weld areas previously chemically treated to assure removal of residual or reformed oxides, if any. Acceptable methods of mechanical cleaning include stainless steel wire brushing, scraping, filing, or sanding. However, abrasives containing iron and its oxides, steel wool and wire, and copper alloy based wire, which may become embedded with galvanically active metals and accelerate corrosion of aluminum alloys shall NOT be used. Mechanical methods shall be vigorous enough to adequately remove any residual oxide films, but gentle enough to avoid forming an excessively rough surface in the comparatively soft metal underneath. 4. description: Residential Reentry Center Services to be Located within either the city limits of Richmond, Virginia; or Henrico County, Virginia; or Chesterfield County, Virginia. Home Confinement Radius: within 100 miles of the facility. The Federal Bureau of Prisons is seeking concerns having the ability for providing Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services (in-house RRC beds) and Home Confinement services (home confinement placements) for male and female Federal offenders held under the authority of United States Statutes which to be located within the city limits of Richmond, Virginia; or Henrico County, Virginia; or Chesterfield County, Virginia. Home Confinement Radius: within 100 miles of the facility. Both the RRC services for in-house RRC beds and the Home Confinement services for home confinement placements shall be in accordance with the Federal Bureau of Prisons Statement of Work (SOW) entitled, �Residential Reentry Center, March, 2022�. Home Confinement services (for home confinement placements) are specifically defined in chapter 10, programs, of the aforementioned SOW. Additional requirements for these services are referenced throughout the SOW as well. This will be a Firm-Fixed Price/IDIQ contract for services with a one-year base period, and four, one-year option period. The RRC In-House requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum of 20 beds for the base year and an estimated maximum of 40 beds (35 males and 5 females). The Home Confinement requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum of 10 placements (for the base year) and an estimated maximum of 20 placements. It is the intent of the Government to award both line items (RRC in-house beds and home confinement placements) to a single provider, as these services are interconnected and rely upon each other to ensure adequate programming and case management of offenders. The Government reserves the right to potentially make an award which is deemed to be in the best interest of the Government. 15BRRC27R00000006 will be available on or about October 30, 2026, and it will be distributed solely through the General Services Administration's Federal Business Opportunities website at https://SAM.gov. description: Amendment 001 to Solicitation #36C25927Q0025 (Air-powered chiropractic tables) This amendment s purpose is to list and answer the questions submitted by the questions deadline as specified in the solicitation. Questions and Answers: CLIN 0018 is listed as "Delivery," but the solicitation states freight shall be added to another line item and not be its own line item. How should offerors handle delivery/freight pricing? Freight costs may be added to the delivery line item if the offeror deems appropriate. Is any on-site installation or assembly required at the SLC or Ogden facilities, or is this delivery of the equipment only? The expectation is that the tables are pre-assembled and will be easy to place in the clinics. However, if the tables are NOT pre-assembled, the offeror should include installation/assembly fees into the delivery line item and ensure it is noted. For an "or equal" product, will an Authorized Distributor Letter from the manufacturer of the equal product we quote satisfy VAAR 852.212-71(c), or must the letter be from Hill Laboratories specifically? The Authorized Distributor Letter must be from the manufacturer of the brand the offeror is proposing. Offerors would only need to provide a letter from Hill Laboratories IF they are offering the Government the Hill Laboratories product. Installation scope: The section is titled "Delivery and Installation," but no installation tasks are listed. Should the price include inside delivery to the treatment room, uncrating, assembly, set-up/leveling, functional testing, packaging and debris removal, and staff in-service training? If so, please name the rooms and floors at each site. The expectation is for the tables to be delivered pre-assembled to the facility. The VA staff would then take possession of the items and move them to the clinic space. The Offeror should include installation/assembly costs IF the tables are not delivered pre-assembled. Delivery windows and access: Please give the allowed delivery days and hours, receiving dock or entrance, elevator access, any check-in or escort steps, and a point of contact at each site (George E. Wahlen VAMC, 500 Foothill Dr., Salt Lake City; Ogden CBOC, 2945 South Washington Blvd., Suite 1, South Ogden). Are deliveries to the 2 sites allowed on different dates? Deliveries may occur on different dates if needed. Deliveries shall be made between 0700 and 1700 Mondays through Fridays (except on Federal holidays). Required delivery date: Is there a required or target delivery date, or a maximum lead time in calendar days after award? A target delivery date is not available. Offerors are encouraged to provide the most accurate delivery lead time possible based on information currently available from the manufacturer. This is an evaluation factor so Offeror s information will be compared. Freight vs. line 0018: The RFQ says freight shall be added to another line item and not be its own line item, but line 0018 is "Delivery." Should delivery/installation be priced on line 0018, or included in line 0001 with 0018 shown as "Included with line item 0001"? Freight costs may be added to the delivery line item if the offeror deems appropriate. If the tables are not pre-assembled, the Offeror will need to include installation/assembly fees in the delivery line item total. *Be sure to make a note that installation/assembly is needed. Removal of existing tables: Is the contractor expected to remove and dispose of any existing tables at either site? If yes, how many, which models, and is there a VA disposal process? No removal or disposal services are required for this requirement. "Or equal" salient characteristics: The RFQ says "air powered - NOT pneumatic or hydraulic." Air-powered systems run on compressed air, which is usually described as pneumatic. Please clarify what this requirement excludes so that "equal" products can be judged fairly. Salient characteristics updated to: Must be air powered/pneumatic NOT hydraulic Option lines: For an "equal" product, may an option that is standard on that product be shown as "Included with line item 0001"? Must each brand-name part number (for example, AF-F15, 92CS, 97) be matched one for one? Each line item does not need to be matched one for one. However, the Offeror should ensure the components listed in the line items are included in the table. Please ensure a note is provided if the brochures/specification documents do not clearly show those items are included with the table. Height and width: Does a maximum height of exactly 29" meet the requirement, and is the 27" width (line 0017) the required width? The tables must be able to reach at least 29 but if the table is able to exceed this height (up to ~ 32 ) that would be preferred. The width dimension of the table must be between 27 and 33 Authorized distributor letter: Is the OEM letter (VAAR 852.212-71(c)) required for all offerors who are not the OEM, including authorized dealers? Must it name this solicitation, or is a general authorization letter on OEM letterhead acceptable? If the Offeror is not the manufacturer of the product they are offering, they must provide an authorized distributor letter from the manufacturer. The letter must be from the manufacturer stating the Offeror is authorized to sell/distribute the manufacturer s product to the Government. The letter may be on letterhead an/or an email but it must clearly be from the manufacturer and specify the Offeror. Contractor access/PIV: Clauses 852.204-70/72 are included, but all risk levels are marked N/a. Please confirm that delivery and installation staff will not need a background check or PIV card, and that a visitor badge and escort is enough? The expectation is for the tables to be pre-assembled and the Offeror would only need to deliver the item to the warehouse dock/facility. No access to the facility is anticipated although the VA staff may accompany the Offeror if delivery/installation/assembly is needed. Warranty/service: Should on-site labor warranty or service be included, or only the minimum 1 year parts warranty? Minimum 1-year parts warranty; additional on-site and/or service warranty appreciated but not mandatory Page limits: The RFQ mentions page limitations but does not state any. Is there a page limit for any volume? No page limits are present for this solicitation. However, Offerors should be mindful of potential email size limitations. Option to Extend Services (52.217-8) and Service Contract Labor Standards (52.222-41/43) are included. Please confirm whether they apply to this one-time supply purchase with installation. FAR 52.217-8 was included in case an extension to the period of performance is needed. SCLS does not apply to this requirement. Deadline time zone. The RFQ states quotes are due 12:00 PM MST on 30 October 2026, while SAM.gov lists the response deadline at UTC-06:00 (MDT). Please confirm the controlling local time for submission. The deadline is 12pm MT on 10/30/2026. Delivery pricing. The instructions state freight shall be added to another line item and not be its own line item, yet the schedule includes line item 0018 "Delivery." Should delivery/freight be priced in line item 0018, or folded into line item 0001 with 0018 marked accordingly? Freight costs may be added to the delivery line item if the offeror deems appropriate. If the tables are not pre-assembled, the Offeror will need to include installation/assembly fees in the delivery line item total. *Be sure to make a note that installation/assembly is needed. Installation. Is installation/set-up of the tables required at either delivery location (Salt Lake City and Ogden), or is delivery only required? If set-up is required, will VA personnel escort access be arranged through the receiving facility? If the tables are pre-assembled, installation shall not be required. However, if assembly of the table is required, the Offeror should include those costs in their quote and should plan to be onsite to i

title: N66001-27-Q-6003 Notice of Intent to Sole Source to Concurrent Technologies Corporation (CAGE Code: 0W151)

The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the USDA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

title: Residential Reentry Center Services to be Located within the Eugene, Oregon; or surrounding areas within Lane County, Oregon. Home Confinement Radius: Within 200-miles of the RRC location.
description: Residential Reentry Center Services to be Located within the Eugene, Oregon; or surrounding areas within Lane County, Oregon. Home Confinement Radius: Within 200-miles of the RRC location. The Federal Bureau of Prisons is seeking concerns having the ability for providing Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services (in-house RRC beds) and Home Confinement services (home confinement placements) for male and female Federal offenders held under the authority of United States Statutes which to be located within the Eugene, Oregon; or surrounding areas within Lane County, Oregon. Home Confinement Radius: Within 200-miles of the RRC location. Both the RRC services for in-house RRC beds and the Home Confinement services for home confinement placements shall be in accordance with the Federal Bureau of Prisons Statement of Work (SOW) entitled, �Residential Reentry Center, March, 2022�. Home Confinement services (for home confinement placements) are specifically defined in chapter 10, programs, of the aforementioned SOW. Additional requirements for these services are referenced throughout the SOW as well. This will be a Firm-Fixed Price/IDIQ contract for services with a one-year base period, and four, one-year option period. The RRC In-House requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum 6 beds (4 males and 2 females) for the base year and an estimated maximum 15 beds (10 males and 5 females) facility. The Home Confinement requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum 2 placements (for the base year) and an estimated maximum 5 placements. It is the intent of the Government to award both line items (RRC in-house beds and home confinement placements) to a single provider, as these services are interconnected and rely upon each other to ensure adequate programming and case management of offenders. PURPOSE: This Source Selection Plan (SSP) outlines the procedures that will be used to solicit architectural and engineering (AE) design services for Project 578-27-003 Renovate A Section on First Floor of Building 1. The goal of this project is to provide complete AE design services to renovate section A of the 1st floor of building 1. 2. ACQUISISTION DESCRIPTION: 2.1: RFI: A Request for Information shall be published to https://sam.gov whereby interested architect-engineering companies shall submit an SF330 package. This competitive procurement shall utilize a best value trade-off source selection process identified in FAR 15. 2.1.a: Source Selection Evaluation Board (SSEB): For the purpose of this acquisition, the SSEB will be same as the Technical Evaluation Board (TEB). 2.1.b: Below are the individual (TEB) evaluation criteria and ratings for the SF330s, listed in descending order of importance. FACTOR 1: SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE AND TECHNICAL COMPETENCE (30 Maximum Points) Subfactor 1A: Specialized Experience (15 Points). Subfactor 1B: Additional Experience (10 points). Subfactor 1C: Technical Competence (5 points). The A/E Firm shall demonstrate its specialized experience and technical competence in the design and construction period services for projects of similar size and complexity. Specialized project experience should include design of renovations to existing hospitals, renovations to buildings constructed prior to 1970 w/space constraints, design of Pathology Suites, and HVAC upgrades to existing hospitals. Additional experience includes mechanical, electrical, and structural engineering, architecture, interior design and finishes, physical security upgrades, building management systems/building automation systems (BMS/BAS), Computer-Aided Design and Drafting (CADD), critical path scheduling, fire protection, construction infection control protocols, design and installation of biological refrigeration and preservation systems, design and installation of vacuum tube transport systems, and project phasing and coordination in an active hospital setting. Offeror shall provide a minimum of three (3), and no more than five (5) recent and relevant Government and private experience projects similar in size, scope, and complexity, and experience with the type of projects/competence above. Relevant is defined as those task requirements identified in the Statement of Work. Recent is defined as services provided within the past seven (7) years with at least 50% of the Construction completed. Project Owner, owner s point of contact including telephone number and email address. Services & Deliverables provided under the contract/task order Period of Performance, including start and completion dates for design and construction if applicable. Estimated cost of construction based on AE s design Final construction cost (or projected final construction cost if still underway) The percentage of total cost resulting from changes due to AE omissions. To demonstrate technical competence, the offeror shall include narratives of how the firm addresses each of the following topics. Simply restating this list will not be sufficient. The management approach The coordination of disciplines and subcontractors Quality control procedures Familiarity with VA Design Guides/Manuals, Master Specifications and other applicable standards. FACTOR 2: PROFESSIONAL QUALIFICATIONS (20 Maximum Points) Subfactor 2A: Key Positions (15 Points). Subfactor 2B: SDVOSB Compliance (5 Points). The architects and engineers on the firm s staff representing the project or signing/stamping drawings in each discipline must possess a minimum of five (5) years of experience and are required to be licensed, registered, or certified by a U.S. state, the District of Columbia, or a U.S. territory. Provide professional license jurisdiction of issue and license numbers and/or proof of licensure. A resume for each of these key positions must be provided, corresponding with the title matching the disciplines listed for the project. At a minimum, the offeror must describe the professional qualifications and specific experience in the required disciplines within the past five (5) years. Key positions and disciplines required for this project include, but are not limited to: Project Manager Architect Mechanical Engineer Electrical Engineer Plumbing Engineer Structural Engineer Interior Designer The evaluation will consider education, certifications, training, registration, overall and relevant experience and longevity with the firm. FACTOR 3: PAST PERFORMANCE (20 Maximum Points) Subfactor 3A: Past Performance of projects identified in FACTOR 1. (15 Points). Subfactor 3B: Average Past Performance of all projects (5 Points). REQUIREMENTS 3.1 Welding and welder qualifications shall be in accordance with AWS D1.1 for steel, AWS D1.2 or MIL-W-22248,Class 4 for aluminum, AWS D1.3 for sheet steel and AWS D1.6 for stainless steel. Proper controls shall be used to prevent melt through or burn through. For aluminum, filler for welding 6061 alloy shall be 4043: filler for welding 5000 series alloys to themselves or to 6061 shall be 5356 or 5556. In addition,welding and weld inspection shall include: (1) Visual inspection shall include 5X (5power) magnification when a suspect condition is to be examined beyond the capability of normal vision. (2) Critical and major welds may be subjected to further non destructive testing (such as dye penetrant inspection)as prescribed by the buying activity. (3) Proper documentation shall be available for review by Government personnel. 3.2 WORK INSTRUCTIONS. Work instructions shall be posted at theoperator's work station giving procedures to control the welding process, i.e., filler material, weld size, electrical and gas characteristics, including flow rate. 3.3 MATERIALS AND MATERIALS CONTROL. The quality program shall assure that the materials used in fabrication or processing, i.e., base metals and weld filler material, be inspected and conform to the applicable physical, chemical and other technical requirements (supplier's certification is sufficient). 3.4 CONTROLS. Weld filler materials shall be clearly identified and segregated from each other both when in storage and at the work station. Work station environment shall be controlled to prevent conditions adverse to proper gas shielding. 3.5 CLEANING. Parts to be welded shall be cleaned to remove surface soils such as oils, waxes, grease, inks, etc. except that uninhibited alkaline solutions such as sodium hydroxide shall NOT be used. 3.6 DEOXIDIZING. The cleaned parts shall be chemically deoxidized NO MORE THAN 10 DAYS PRIOR TO WELDING to remove thick surface oxide films. (If the material or work is exposed to an outdoor environment, this time limit shall be reduced to a maximum of 3 days, to account for atmospheric effects.) Mechanical cleaning methods shall be applied just prior to the actual start of welding, to remove any reoxidation or residual thin oxide films. 3.6.1 CHEMICAL TREATMENT. An acid deoxidizing treatment shall be applied by either immersion or brushing/wiping. Deoxidizers acceptable for use shall include nitric acid, sulfuric chromic, phosphoric chromic, or equivalent solutions. Sodium hydroxide solutions shall not be used. Care shall be taken to assure 100% solution coverage of the area to be welded. To allow an adequately sized deoxidized area for good welding, the solution shall be applied to an area extending at least 2 inches from the weld site, or ending at any closer adjacent edge. 3.6.2 MECHANICAL MEANS. Immediately prior to welding, mechanical cleaning methods shall be applied to the weld areas previously chemically treated to assure removal of residual or reformed oxides, if any. Acceptable methods of mechanical cleaning include stainless steel wire brushing, scraping, filing, or sanding. However, abrasives containing iron and its oxides, steel wool and wire, and copper alloy based wire, which may become embedded with galvanically active metals and accelerate corrosion of aluminum alloys shall NOT be used. Mechanical methods shall be vigorous enough to adequately remove any residual oxide films, but gentle enough to avoid forming an excessively rough surface in the comparatively soft metal underneath. 4. If the firm is not registered in SAM, you may register online at https://www.sam.gov. 1. PURPOSE: This Source Selection Plan (SSP) outlines the procedures that will be used to solicit architectural and engineering (AE) design services for Project 578-27-003 Renovate A Section on First Floor of Building 1. The goal of this project is to provide complete AE design services to renovate section A of the 1st floor of building 1. 2. ACQUISISTION DESCRIPTION: 2.1: RFI: A Request for Information shall be published to https://sam.gov whereby interested architect-engineering companies shall submit an SF330 package. This competitive procurement shall utilize a best value trade-off source selection process identified in FAR 15. 2.1.a: Source Selection Evaluation Board (SSEB): For the purpose of this acquisition, the SSEB will be same as the Technical Evaluation Board (TEB). 2.1.b: Below are the individual (TEB) evaluation criteria and ratings for the SF330s, listed in descending order of importance. FACTOR 1: SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE AND TECHNICAL COMPETENCE (30 Maximum Points) Subfactor 1A: Specialized Experience (15 Points). Subfactor 1B: Additional Experience (10 points). Subfactor 1C: Technical Competence (5 points). The A/E Firm shall demonstrate its specialized experience and technical competence in the design and construction period services for projects of similar size and complexity. Specialized project experience should include design of renovations to existing hospitals, renovations to buildings constructed prior to 1970 w/space constraints, design of Pathology Suites, and HVAC upgrades to existing hospitals. Additional experience includes mechanical, electrical, and structural engineering, architecture, interior design and finishes, physical security upgrades, building management systems/building automation systems (BMS/BAS), Computer-Aided Design and Drafting (CADD), critical path scheduling, fire protection, construction infection control protocols, design and installation of biological refrigeration and preservation systems, design and installation of vacuum tube transport systems, and project phasing and coordination in an active hospital setting. Recent is defined as services provided within the past seven (7) years with at least 50% of the Construction completed. Services & Deliverables provided under the contract/task order Period of Performance, including start and completion dates for design and construction if applicable. Estimated cost of construction based on AE s design Final construction cost (or projected final construction cost if still underway) The percentage of total cost resulting from changes due to AE omissions. To demonstrate technical competence, the offeror shall include narratives of how the firm addresses each of the following topics. Simply restating this list will not be sufficient. The management approach The coordination of disciplines and subcontractors Quality control procedures Familiarity with VA Design Guides/Manuals, Master Specifications and other applicable standards.
