title: Y--NGWSP Cutter Lateral Reach 21 Booster Plant
description: Pre-Solicitation Notice: NGWSP Cutter Lateral Reach 21 Booster Plant PURPOSE: The U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, Upper Colorado Basin Region, Four Corners Construction Office (FCCO), is issuing this pre-solicitation notice for a contemplated construction project titled: Navajo Gallup Water Supply Project (NGWSP) Cutter Lateral Reach 21 Booster Plant. This requirement is being procured in accordance with Part 14 of the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) with a set-aside for small businesses. The Bureau of Reclamation intends to issue a competitive solicitation for this requirement. Based on market research it was determined that there were a sufficient number of qualified small businesses with sufficient bonding capacity to perform as the prime contractor on this project, and as such, it is anticipated to be set-aside for small businesses. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The Navajo Gallup Water Supply Project (NGWSP) is a major infrastructure project that once constructed, will convey a reliable municipal and industrial water supply from the San Juan River to the eastern section of the Navajo Nation, southwestern portion of the Jicarilla Apache Nation, and the city of Gallup, New Mexico via approximately 280 miles of pipeline, several pumping plants, and two water treatment plants. The principal components of work for the Cutter Lateral Reach 21 Booster Plant include, but are not limited to, the following: 1. Pre-engineered concrete booster pump station, concrete foundation pad, pipe encasement, yard pipe, fencing, electrical equipment, gravel surfacing, and pipe connections. 2. Installation of secondary regulation tank at Regulation Tank No. 3 site, foundation, electrical equipment, yard pipe, and pipe connections. 3. Erosion and scour restoration/prevention: a. Includes a retaining wall, swale, runoff channel, and site regrading. 4. Reinstallation of gravel surfacing at Regulation Tank No. 3 site. 5. Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) equipment and radio communications system. LOCATION OF THE WORK: The NGWSP Cutter Lateral Reach 21 booster plant is located approximately 26 miles South of Bloomfield, NM off County Road 7575 near U.S. Highway 550, at the base of Huerfano Mesa in San Juan County, New Mexico. NAICS AND SIZE STANDARD: The NAICS code for this project is 237110 (Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures Construction) with a small business size standard of $45.0 million. COMPETITION: Solicitation 140R4026B0003 is anticipated to be conducted as a small business set-aside. The project specifications and project location will be defined in the solicitation document. The solicitation will require a bid guarantee of at least 20% of the bid price. The Contract will require payment and performance bonds for 100% of the contract price. Offerors must have sufficient bonding capacity. DISCLOSURE OF THE MAGNITUDE OF THE CONSTRUCTION PROJECT: The magnitude of this project is between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000. SOLICITATION RELEASE DATE: All responsible sources may submit a proposal which shall be considered by the agency. A free, electronic copy of the solicitation will be available on APPROXIMATELY November 2, 2026, at https://www.sam.gov/. Simply type in solicitation number "140R4026B0003" in the Keyword / Solicitation # field. A draft solicitation for comment has been attached to this announcement. The purpose of the draft solicitation is for comments only. When comments are received and incorporated, the solicitation will be posted requesting the submission of proposals. This project will follow a best-value procurement process under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 14. Questions and comments must be submitted in writing by e-mail to Philoma Singer at philoma_singer@ios.doi.gov and Tyler Spencer, at tyler_spencer@ios.doi.gov. SYSTEM FOR AWARD MANAGEMENT (SAM, www.sam.gov): The System for Award Management (SAM) is a recently implemented Federal Government owned-and-operated FREE web site that consolidates the capabilities in Central Contractor Registration (CCR)/Federal Register (FedReg), Online Representations and Certifications Application (ORCA), and Excluded Parties List System (EPLS). Offerors must be successfully registered in SAM in order to be considered for a government contract award. If you had an active record in CCR, you have an active record in SAM. SITE VISIT: The Government intends to conduct a site visit for highly interested vendors AROUND November 12, 2026. Information regarding the site visit will be in Section L of the solicitation once released. POINT-OF-CONTACT FOR QUESTIONS: The Contract Specialist for this solicitation is Philoma Singer at philoma_singer@ios.doi.gov. The Contracting Officer for this solicitation is Tyler Spencer, tyler_spencer@ios.doi.gov. Any communication regarding this procurement must be made in writing and forwarded via email and must identify the solicitation number, company name, address, email address, phone number including area code, and point of contact. Emails shall be addressed to the Contract Specialist and cc the Contracting Officer. NOTE: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (SOLICITATION), AN INVITATION FOR BID (IFB), NOR IS IT A REQUEST FOR QUOTATION (RFQ). It is not to be construed as a commitment by the requesting party to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. Responses will not be considered as proposals, bids, or quotes. No award will be made as a result of this Notice. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by interested parties in responding to this Notice. This FedBizOps Notice is strictly for compliance with FAR Subpart 5.2. As a result of this Notice, the Government may issue a competitive solicitation; however, should such requirements materialize, no basis for claims against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to the Notice (e.g. use of such information as either part of its evaluation process or in developing specifications for any subsequent requirement). description: Sources Sought Notice Sources Sought Notice Page 5 of 5 Sources Sought Notice *= Required Field Sources Sought Notice Page 1 of 5 The VA Saint Louis Health Care System, John Cochran Division, requires a Construction Contractor to replace various roofs identified through FCA report. Title: 657-26-102JC FCA Replace Various Roofs on BLDG 1, JC Solicitation Number: 36C25527R0012 Contracting Office: Network Contracting Office 15 Contracting Office Location: 3450 S 4th Street Traffic way, Leavenworth, Kansas Posted Date: 10/22/2026 Response Date: 10/30/2026 at 2:00 PM Central Time Set Aside: Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business Classification Code: Z2DA - Repair or Alteration of Hospitals and Infirmaries NAICS Code: 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction Synopsis: Please note that this is NOT a request for quotes or proposals, the Government is seeking information for market research purposes only. The Government may or may not issue solicitation documents. The Department of Veterans Affairs Network Contracting Office (NCO) 15, is conducting a market survey for qualified: Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB), capable of providing the required services outlined below for the John Cochran VA Medical Center, Saint Louis, Missouri. The applicable NAICS code is 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction and the size standard is $45.0 Million. Responses to this notice must be submitted via e-mail and received no later than October 30, 2026, at 2:00 PM Central Time. No telephone inquiries will be accepted or returned. Additional information about this project will be issued on the Federal Contract Opportunities website https://www.sam.gov once available. Period of Performance for all work is 180 calendar days. In accordance with FAR 36.204, the estimated cost magnitude is between $1,000,000.00 and $5,000,000.00 Prospective SDVOSB firms are reminded that in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.219-14(e)(3), the Contractor agrees it will not pay more than 85 percent of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance, excluding the cost of materials, to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities. Any work that a similarly situated entity further subcontracts will count towards the prime contractor's 85 percent subcontract amount that cannot be exceeded. GENERAL SCOPE OF WORK: Work includes, but is not limited to, general construction, alterations, mechanical, electrical & plumbing work, utility systems, fire protection systems, abatement work, necessary demolition and removal of existing structures, associated appurtenances, and certain other items necessary completion. All work shall be performed in accordance with solicitation/contract terms and conditions, specifications and drawings, and all applicable VA TIL and local and National codes. Contractor shall furnish all supervision, tools, labor, materials, equipment, transportation and testing necessary. Contractor will perform site investigations to fully inform themselves of the conditions and limitations applied to the work. The drawings and specifications include guidance on: Working hours allowed on this project. ICRA (Infection Control Risk Assessments) requirements and containment barriers. ILSM (Interim Life Safety Measures). Division of responsibilities between contractor and equipment vendor. This Statement of Work (SOW) is intended as an outline and is not a detailed summary of the work the contractor will be required to perform. In the event of conflict between this SOW and the project drawings and specifications, the drawings and specifications will take precedence over this SOW. The project will be completed within 210 calendar days from receipt of Notice to Proceed (NTP). END OF SCOPE OF WORK Interested firms must be registered in https://sam.gov with NAICS code 236220 and qualified as a Service Disabled Veteran Owned small business under 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. Qualified service-disabled veteran owned small businesses are encouraged to respond and required to be registered in with the Small Business Administration (SBA) registry https://veterans.certify.sba.gov on or before the response date. If interested in this opportunity, please provide Capability Statement via email. The Capability Statement is designed to inform the Department of Veteran Affairs of any prospective construction contractors' project execution capabilities. The submission is limited to 10 pages which shall include the following information: 1) Offeror's name, address, point of contact, phone number, e-mail address, and Unique Entity ID. 2) Offeror's interest in bidding on the solicitation when it is issued. 3) Offeror's capability to perform a contract of this magnitude and complexity and comparable work performed within the past 5 years - brief description of the project, customer name, timeliness of performance, customer satisfaction, and dollar value of the project - provide at least 1, but no more than 3 completed construction examples. 4) Offeror's CVE certification as a Veteran owned business. 5) Please provide Socio-economic status for NAICS code 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction and provide percentage of self-performed labor your company can perform for this type of project. 6) Offeror's Joint Venture information if applicable - existing and potential. 7) Offeror's Bonding Capability in the form of a letter from Surety providing bonding level per contract and aggregate. title: P7777 ACC SARP Replacement NAS Jacksonville, Florida - AMAG Access Control Equipment panel
description: Notice of intent to use a brand name product. The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Southeast (NAVFAC SE) is performing a market survey to determine if other potential sources of supply can provide an access control equipment panels that has equal performance and that can fully integrate with the existing AMAG Symmetry Enterprise video surveillance system as the AMAG M2150-2DBC, M2150-4DBC, M2150-DBU/MKII, and M2150-8DBC/MKII manufactured by AMAG Technology, 2205 W. 126th Street Unit B, Hawthorne, CA 90250. Fiscal Year 2027 PROJECT P7777 ACC SARP Replacement NAS Jacksonville, Florida, requires the following characteristics. Provide access control equipment panel with the following capabilities: Must fully integrate into the existing AMAG Symmetry Enterprise access control system to include all software, hardware, database, and licensing. Connects to AMAG Symmetry management software via LAN Can control up to 16 doors per equipment panel Can manage 20,000 card holders and 65,000 offline transactions (expandable to 250,000) Connect smart card, proximity readers Wiegand support using WIM UL 294 and UL 1076 listed 100 Mbps network connection Input and output modules This notification is for market research purposes only to identify if other potential sources of supply can meet the requirements of the Government. This is not a request for proposals, quotes, or an invitation for bid. The intent of this notice is to identify other potential sources of this product. To be considered, please submit detailed technical data for the Government to conduct a comprehensive evaluation of your manufactured product to ensure compatibility with the existing system. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), a response to this notice is not an offer and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The responder is solely responsible for the information it submits and any associated costs. The Government reserves the right to disregard any submittal that is incomplete or vague. Please do not submit company brochures. Please limit your submissions to five (5) one-sided pages, not including the cover or table of contents pages. In addition, Attachment 1 must be included with your submission, and does not count against the page limit. Please submit complete information via electronic mail to Reuben Amarh reuben.a.amarh.civ@us.navy.mil and Jeff Rhein at jeffrey.j.rhein.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 30 OCT 2026 at 3:00 PM ET. Any information received after the due date/time will not be considered. Any information provided to the Government in response to this RFI will become U.S. Government property. All proprietary or classified information will be treated appropriately. Questions and Responses: Questions concerning this sources sought notice must be submitted no later than the response deadline of 23 OCT 2026 not later than 3:00 PM ET. The Government may, at its discretion, respond to questions received before that deadline. Questions received after the deadline may not be considered or answered. As of 21 OCT 2026, the Government has received responses based on the information currently published. Information material to the market-research response will not be provided exclusively to one respondent. If the Government determines that additional clarification is appropriate, anonymized questions and Government responses will be posted through an update to this notice. Contractor names and proprietary or confidential information will not be disclosed. If a posted clarification materially changes the information requested or the anticipated requirement, the Government may extend the response deadline and permit respondents to submit revised or supplemental information. Additional technical or acquisition details that are not currently available may be addressed in a future solicitation, if one is issued.

title: FA8501-27-RAPID-PAVE-OTA
description: The Department of the Air Force, 78th Civil Engineer Group, Robins Air Force Base, Georgia, is issuing this Special Notice under the Robins Agile Practices for Infrastructure Development (RAPID) umbrella framework and pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The Government seeks industry Solution Briefs for an anticipated Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) to restore, modernize, and sustain critical airfield infrastructure at Robins Air Force Base. The requirement includes airfield pavement, runway-overrun, taxiway, drainage, pavement marking, and associated supporting work necessary to improve safe, reliable, and mission-ready aircraft operations. This Special Notice is not an invitation for bids, a request for proposals under the Federal Acquisition Regulation, nor a commitment by the Government to make an award. Any resulting instrument will be an OTA for facility construction and repair under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Purpose The purpose of this Area of Interest is to obtain commercially viable, safe, and schedule-credible solutions to restore and sustain airfield infrastructure supporting safe aircraft movement, installation readiness, and continued mission operations at Robins Air Force Base, Georgia. The Government requires an integrated approach to address deteriorated pavement, runway overrun, taxiway, drainage, storm-drain-disposal, pavement-marking, and related airfield infrastructure conditions. The selected approach must provide a practical path to execute the work while minimizing disruption to aircraft operations and controlling construction, safety, environmental, and schedule risks. Project Background and Existing Conditions The current runway and taxiway infrastructure exhibit deterioration, including cracking, displacement, rutting, and other pavement deficiencies that affect long-term serviceability and air-field-operational reliability. Drainage infrastructure near the south end of the runway is overgrown and requires adjustment or corrective work to improve drainage performance and reduce the risk of continued pavement or operational impacts. The work area is congested and affected by ongoing airfield operations, access restrictions, construction staging limitations, and mission requirements. The runway and taxiway may remain in full or partial operation depending on the approved phase of work. Project Areas UHHZ210404: Runway 3901 Pavement and Shoulders The Government requires a solution to address deficiencies associated with Runway 3901 pavement slabs, shoulders, pavement condition, and associated maintenance and marking requirements. The desired end state is a safe, serviceable runway with restored pavement integrity, shoulders, markings, and supporting features necessary for continued airfield operations. UHHZ210404: South Runway Overrun The Government requires a solution to replace or restore the south runway overrun and associated infrastructure necessary to support safe runway operations. Respondents shall address proposed sequencing, access, staging, safety controls, airfield coordination, and methods for reducing operational disruption. UHHZ210404: South Overrun Contingency Work The Government may include additional south-overrun work as a contingent requirement. Respondents shall identify assumptions, cost and schedule impacts, technical dependencies, and proposed activation conditions associated with any contingent work. The Government will determine whether this work is included in the final OTA scope, separately negotiated, or otherwise addressed during Phase 3. UHHZ150412: Taxiway C, Facility 3931 The Government requires a solution to repair Taxiway C, Facility 3931, and restore safe, reliable aircraft ground-movement capability. The proposed approach should address pavement condition, phasing, aircraft-operational coordination, quality control, inspection, testing, and turnover requirements. UHHZ160138: Drainage and Storm-Drain Disposal, Facility 8700 The Government requires a solution to correct drainage and storm-drain-disposal deficiencies at Facility 8700. The proposed approach should address existing drainage conditions, water management, constructability, site access, protection of adjacent infrastructure, environmental controls, and integration with related pavement and airfield work. OTA & RAPID Framework Approach This project is being executed as an Area of Interest (AOI) under the overarching RAPID (Robins Agile Practices for Infrastructure Development) Umbrella Program Notice. In accordance with the RAPID framework, this project utilizes a Build-Only execution approach under the standalone statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Because the Government has provided a 100% completed design package and/or specific phasing and repair requirements, this project does not contain a collaborative design-builder phase. Instead, it transitions directly to rapid construction execution under an OTA structure to bypass administrative procurement lag. Competitive Selection Process Phase 1 Solution Brief Requirements The Government reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to determine that a response which does not conform to the requirements or instructions contained in this announcement is ineligible for further consideration. Interested respondents shall submit a Phase 1 Solution Brief in a clear, concise, and organized manner in accordance with this announcement. To facilitate an efficient review, responses shall be prepared in accordance with the instructions and formatting requirements contained in this announcement. Failure to comply with these requirements may increase the risk that the response will not be considered for further evaluation. The Government will evaluate them to identify the most highly qualified parties. Submission Requirement should be submitted by 3:00 PM Eastern Standard Time on or before 30 October 2026. Interested respondents shall submit a Phase 1 Solution Brief consisting of no more than five written pages (5), excluding the cover page. The Solution Brief shall include: Cover Page Company name UEI Mailing address Primary point of contact Email address and telephone number Identification of this RAPID AOI Executive Summary, Team Composition, and Organization Summary of the respondent�s qualifications and anticipated delivery capability Explanation of why the team is qualified for the anticipated requirement The team�s understanding of the Robins Air Force Base operational environment The team�s experience working in operational, secure, airfield, industrial, or similarly constrained environments The team�s proposed approach to Phase 1 collaboration and risk reduction Identification of any material capability, staffing, access, bonding, or teaming assumptions. Past Relevant Construction Capability and Experience Minimum Requirement: The Company must demonstrate a minimum of five (5) years of experience successfully executing construction projects of comparable size, scope, and complexity. Contractors must have previous experience on Government runway/ taxiway projects that entail repair or replacement or new construction Focus: Historical performance in occupied facilities, managing congested site logistics, working in restricted areas (e.g., flightlines), and adhering to environmental and safety standards. Financial Capacity and Bonding A statement of financial capacity to perform the anticipated work Current single-project and aggregate bonding capacity, if bonds are anticipated; Name of surety Any other information necessary to demonstrate capacity to perform the anticipated project. Construction Execution and Phasing Approach Technical understanding of the 100% Government-furnished design Methodology for physical work execution Utility outage coordination The realism of the proposed master schedule Evaluation & Selection Criteria The Government will utilize a two-step, Best-Value selection process mapped to the RAPID framework to select the Company. title: Generation and Delivery of Meteorological and Hydrological Forecasts for the Western Washington and Northwest Montana River Basins
description: The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Seattle District, intends to issue a firm-fixed-price purchase order on a sole source basis to Upstream Tech for commercial hydrologic and meteorological forecasting services. These services support the Water Management Section�s critical missions for the Green, White/Puyallup, and Kootenai River basins, which include standard reservoir regulation, seasonal water supply forecasting, dam safety, and real-time emergency flood-fighting operations. This requirement will be procured in accordance with RFO 12.102(a), which allows for solicitation from a single source when the contracting officer determines that only one source is reasonably available. The Product Service Code for this requirement is R427 (Support � Professional: Weather Reporting/Observation) and the NAICS code is 541990 (All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services), with a size standard of $19.5 million. The Government has determined that Upstream Tech is the only source capable of providing the required services without unacceptable disruption, mission risk, and substantial duplication of cost. The required services include the generation and delivery of high-resolution, basin-specific meteorological and hydrological forecast data feeds. Market research confirms that Upstream Tech has unique qualifications, as its proprietary forecasting models, analytical tools, and automated data pipelines are deeply integrated into the District's daily water management operating procedures and Corps Water Management System (CWMS). A transition to an alternative vendor would require an estimated 12 to 18 months to develop, calibrate, and validate new models, which would introduce unacceptable risks to public safety and dam safety operations. This notice is not a request for competitive quotes. Information received will normally be considered for the purpose of identifying small business vendors with the capability to fulfill the requirement. The Government will not pay for any information received. Any firm that believes it can provide the stated service can provide supporting documents demonstrating their capabilities and specifications. Information received will be used primarily for market research purposes to determine the feasibility of competition for future requirements. Information can be sent to the Contract Specialist, Dwain Graham, at dwain.m.graham@usace.army.mil. This procurement will be made in accordance with RFO FAR Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services.

title: TAC Robotic Process Automation Training
description: 1.0 BACKGROUND This request for information is for market research purposes only in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) Part 10 procedures. This is not a solicitation, nor does it guarantee a solicitation will be issued. Requests for a solicitation will not receive a response. This is not a request for proposals, and it does not obligate the government in any manner. The mission of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Procurement, Acquisition, and Logistics, Technology Acquisition Center (TAC) is to support our Nation�s Veterans by providing acquisition and logistics solutions for VA. In meeting these goals, TAC is responsible for preparing and executing quality contracts that support the Information Technology (IT) efforts and needs of its customers across VA, which enables our customers to provide best value solutions to Veterans and their families. TAC employees are forward-thinking, smart, and innovative acquisition professionals, with strong technical and leadership competencies. To continue to offer our customers customized and responsive service, maintain nimble operations, and provide expert technical support services, TAC must ensure its workforce continues to enhance and maintain knowledge and awareness across a variety of current and emerging IT technologies and trends. The TAC seeks to expand workforce awareness and readiness for Robotic Process Automation (RPA). This training shall be for up to three-days, predominantly informational and demonstration-driven course provides foundational understanding of RPA, VA-aligned use cases, and a limited hands-on component to reinforce learning. 2.0 TRAINING REQUIREMENTS The TAC has a requirement for RPA training to be delivered to its workforce. Facilitation � All training courses shall be �live,� virtual, instructor led training delivered in real-time and not pre-recorded or self-paced. Schedule � All training shall be delivered in Fiscal Year 2025 between October 1, 2026, through June 30, 2027. No training is permitted during 4th quarter of the Fiscal Year. The Contractor is responsible for coordinating a final training schedule in accordance with the requirements in this notice for approval by the Government within two (2) weeks of the training start date. Course Content � Contractors shall effectively utilize demos, knowledge checks, and hands-on learning activities as appropriate. The training courses shall include up-to-date training material on the latest versions of the latest products. Students should be provided with or have access to view, listen, and/or print all course content. Course content shall be available online to students in video, audio and/or written transcript formats. Changes � The Contractor shall accommodate student changes within 24-hours of the start of any training class session. Changes include student drop-out, student additions, and student switches. It does not include additional students beyond the stated student maximums. Technical Support � The Contractor shall be always available during the course. Section 508 � The training shall meet Section 508 compliance standards TRAINING DELIVERABLES All deliverables shall be in a standardized format. Kick-off Meeting and Course Schedule (Deliverable 1) The Contractor shall conduct a kick-off meeting within one (1) week of contract award with the Government POCs. The Contractor shall coordinate a final course schedule for approval by the Government. The Contractor shall coordinate a final Training Schedule with draft course curriculum in accordance with the requirements of this PWS for approval by the Government. 2. Welcome Letter / Course Curriculum and Training Materials (Deliverable 2) The Contractor shall provide the Course Curriculum and Training Materials to the Government POCs no later than two weeks prior to the scheduled start date of the training course. The Course Curriculum and Training Materials shall include the course agenda, learning objectives, presentation materials, and materials for practical exercises, case studies, and job aids, as applicable. The Contractor shall be responsible for coordinating with the Government point of contract (POC) to release a welcome letter and virtual training invites to all attendees within three (3) days prior to the start of the training. 3. Attendee Roster (Deliverable 3) The Contractor shall take attendance for each training course and provide an attendance sheet to the Government delivery POCs. The attendee roster shall include the name, email, and timestamps of the attendees. Training that is multi-day shall have attendance taken each day. Training course attendance is estimated to be 20- 25 students per class. 4. Certificate of Completion (Deliverable 4) The Contractor shall coordinate with the designated Government POC for Continuous Learning Points (CLPs) approval with all awarded training. Training that extends for a working day (including lunch and breaks) shall be 8 CLPs per full day. The Contractor shall email a certificate of completion to each student within one (1) week of course completion. Certificates of Completion shall include, at a minimum, the name of the training course, training date(s), instructor, Contractor�s name, student�s name, and number of CLPs earned. 5. Feedback Survey (Deliverable 5) The Contractor shall collect training feedback from attendees upon completion of each training course. Feedback shall be provided to the Government delivery POC within three (3) weeks of the training course completion. Feedback information shall be organized and clearly presented. 3.0 SPECIFIC TASKS 3.1 INFORMATIONAL FOUNDATIONS & CONCEPTUAL UNDERSTANDING The Contractor shall deliver an instructor-led session introducing RPA fundamentals, VA use cases, and automation value. Tasks � Explain what RPA is, how bots follow rules, and how automation aligns with VA mission needs. � Demonstrate VA-aligned RPA workflows to build conceptual understanding. � Introduce core criteria for automation suitability (rules-based, repetitive, high-volume). � Discuss VA Tools for RPA such as UiPath, Blue Prism, and the use of VA RPA Platform. Deliverables Presentation deck Demonstration scripts and recordings 3.2 DEMONSTRATION-DRIVEN WORKFLOW DEEP-DIVE The Contractor shall conduct demo-intensive instruction deep-diving into RPA workflow design and operations. Tasks � Demonstrate step-by-step bot logic (triggers, rules, decisions, exception handling, audit logging). � Show operational dashboards for monitoring and orchestrating workflows. � Provide narrated, multi-step RPA workflow walk-throughs relevant to VA operations. Deliverables Demo walkthrough documentation Workflow visualizations 3.3 BOT SUITABILITY MODULE, GROUP BRAINSTORMING, AND GUIDED MINI-LAB USING MICROSOFT POWER AUTOMATE 3.3.1 BOT-SUITABILITY INSTRUCTION MODULE Teach class how to evaluate whether a process is appropriate for automation. � Characteristics of strong candidates: repetitive, rules-driven, structured inputs, high volume, stable decisions. � Characteristics of poor candidates: subjective judgment, frequently changing workflows, unstructured/inaccessible data. � VA-specific considerations: data sensitivity, compliance, system constraints. Deliverables Bot Suitability Evaluation Guide VA-aligned suitability checklist 3.3.2 BRAINSTORMING SESSION (TALK, DEMO, GROUP EXERCISE) Conduct a structured session to identify RPA opportunities. � Talk: Explain problem identification, workflow pain-points, and target improvements. � Demo: Decompose a VA process into discrete steps and map to automation criteria; present impact-effort examples. � Group Exercise: Small groups brainstorm tasks, define current and target states, validate against suitability criteria. Deliverables Brainstorming exercises packet Group-generated candidate list Completed impact-effort matrices 3.3.3 GUIDED MINI-LAB USING MICROSOFT POWER AUTOMATE (HANDS-ON) Provide a limited, tightly structured hands-on activi

description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Philadelphia District, intends to award a Firm-Fixed Price, Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Single Award Task Order Contract (SATOC) for Preventative Maintenance and Repair of Heavy Equipment for the Fort Mifflin Project Office within the USACE Philadelphia (NAP) District area of responsibility in accordance with the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS). The Contractor is responsible for scheduling work in accordance with the requirements of task order issued and during regular business hours when scheduling on site work. The site conducts regular business from 7:00am to 3:00pm, Monday through Friday, except for federal holidays. All work is to be performed during these regular business hours. Any hours to be worked outside of the regular business hours shall be coordinated with the COR. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform preventative maintenance and repair of heavy equipment for the Fort Mifflin Project Office as defined in this Performance Work Statement except for those items specified as government furnished property and services. The contractor shall perform to the standards in this contract. The Fort Mifflin Project Office is responsible for the construction of the district�s disposal areas located along the Delaware River. Our mission supports the deepening and the maintenance dredging of the Delaware River and Wilmington Harbor. Heavy Equipment is utilized to construct dikes, ditching for drying and other dirt work. Our equipment is currently composed of D6 Dozers, Excavators (tracks and pontoons), dump trucks (articulated). Without equipment to provide the necessary dirt work in these disposals� areas, dredging assignments in the Delaware Harbor could not be accomplished. It is important that dredging and proper disposal activities of dredge materials is accomplished because it directly effects commerce and the safety of vessels transporting commodities and other resources to the ports. See attachment labeled "W912BU26QA024_FMPO Combined Solicitation Synopsis.pdf" with the requirements of this RFQ and other attachments required for informational and submission purposes.

title: P7777 ACC SARP Replacement NAS Jacksonville, Florida - Accurate Lock & Hardware
description: Notice of intent to use a brand name product. The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Southeast (NAVFAC SE) is performing a market survey to determine if other potential sources of supply can provide a ligature-resistant sliding door system that has equal performance to the LR-SDS / SL-LR-SDS, manufactured by Accurate Lock & Hardware, 1 Annie Place, Stamford, CT 06902. Fiscal Year 2027 PROJECT P7777 ACC SARP Replacement NAS Jacksonville, Florida, requires the following characteristics. Provide ligature-resistant sliding door system with the following capabilities: Ligature-Resistant Design � A sliding door system specifically designed for behavioral health environments that eliminates ligature opportunities associated with conventional swinging doors, including the top edge of the door and side latch locations. The system shall utilize a concealed overhead track, concealed locking hardware, ligature-resistant operating trim, and concealed vertical rod locking or latching mechanisms with no exposed anchor points or accessible cavities. Threshold and Floor Guide � An anti-barricade floor guide that allows sliding operation without creating additional ligature points. Optional threshold/transom assemblies shall be available to reduce the bottom door gap while allowing emergency access and maintaining safe operation. Safety and Security Features � The system shall reduce opportunities for patient barricading, prevent the door from being used as a swinging weapon, and provide staff override capability for all interior locking functions. Locking functions shall include behavioral health applications such as classroom, storeroom, and self-latching patient room configurations. Performance Requirements � The system shall: Meet or exceed a 150 ft-lb impact test in accordance with ANSI A250.13-2014, Section 6.1.1.2. Continue to function following impact testing. Utilize dual ball-bearing carrier assemblies rated at 1,240 lbs dynamic load capacity each. Where required, comply with ANSI/UL 1784 air leakage testing with measured leakage substantially below the allowable code limit. Unique Product Characteristics � The system incorporates proprietary concealed track, locking, and staff-override hardware specifically developed for behavioral healthcare applications. The integrated design combines ligature resistance, anti-barricade functionality, smoke-control capability (where required), and behavioral health locking functions within a single system. The LR-SDS has also been evaluated by the New York State Office of Mental Health and is included in the OMH Patient Safety Guidelines. This notification is for market research purposes only to identify if other potential sources of supply can meet the requirements of the Government. This is not a request for proposals, quotes, or an invitation for bid. The intent of this notice is to identify other potential sources of this product. To be considered, please submit detailed technical data for the Government to conduct a comprehensive evaluation of your manufactured product to ensure compatibility with the existing system. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), a response to this notice is not an offer and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The responder is solely responsible for the information it submits and any associated costs. The Government reserves the right to disregard any submittal that is incomplete or vague. Please do not submit company brochures. Please limit your submissions to five (5) one-sided pages, not including the cover or table of contents pages. In addition, Attachment 1 must be included with your submission, and does not count against the page limit. Please submit complete information via electronic mail to Reuben Amarh reuben.a.amarh.civ@us.navy.mil and Jeff Rhein at jeffrey.j.rhein.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 30 OCT 2026 at 3:00 PM ET. Any information received after the due date/time will not be considered. Any information provided to the Government in response to this RFI will become U.S. Government property. All proprietary or classified information will be treated appropriately.
